raw_case_text:
An 18-year-old female presented to our hospital with chief complaints of progressive fatigue, fever, myalgia, and shortness of breath for last 3 weeks. There was no significant past illness. There was no history of significant weight loss, cough, orthopnea, pain abdomen. On physical examination, she was febrile, pale, and icteric. The spleen was palpable 2 cm below the left costal margin. Her pulse rate was 102/minute with a blood pressure of 106/70 mmHg.
A complete blood count (CBC) revealed severe anemia (hemoglobin:5.8 g/dl, mean corpuscular volume (MCV):92 fl) with a platelet count of 148 x 103/microL and white blood cell count (WBC) of 3.37 x 103/microL. A peripheral blood smear showed few spherocytes, nucleated red blood cells. Biochemistry showed indirect hyperbilirubinemia with high lactate dehydrogenase (LDH:1540 IU/L). On further investigations, corrected reticulocyte count was 5.4%. A direct Coombs test was strongly positive (4+). Based on initial investigations, we made an initial diagnosis of autoimmune hemolytic anemia. Viral markers (HIV, HBs Ag, anti-HCV) were negative. Serology for Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) and mycoplasma was also negative. Antinuclear antibodies were absent. Our patient remained febrile during hospitalisation, which was not explained by hemolytic anemia; on further evaluation, there was a recent history of consumption of unpasteurized milk. Since Brucella is one of the common zoonotic diseases in western India, we suspected brucellosis. The serology for brucellosis was positive in high titre (standard agglutination test:1:640). The diagnosis was confirmed with positive blood culture for Brucella melitensis. We made a final diagnosis of acute brucellosis with Coombs-positive hemolytic anemia. The patient was prescribed a combination of oral doxycycline (100 mg twice a day) with rifampicin (600 mg once a day). She was also prescribed corticosteroids (prednisolone 1 mg/kg/day). 1 week after starting steroids, the patient showed significant clinical improvement with a hemoglobin count of 9 gm/dl and serum LDH of 988 IU/L. The patient was discharged, and steroid was gradually tapered with doxycycline, and rifampicin was advised for further 5 weeks. After 6 weeks, corticosteroid was tapered successfully. The patient was symptomatically better with a hemoglobin count of 13 gm/dl (Figure 1). She was doing well with complete remission of hemolytic anemia at 3-month follow-up.

subjective.chief_complaint: An 18-year-old female presented with a 3-week history of progressive fatigue, fever, myalgia, and shortness of breath.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient presented with a 3-week history of worsening fatigue, high-grade fever, diffuse myalgias, and exertional shortness of breath. She denied cough, orthopnea, abdominal pain, or significant weight loss. She remained persistently febrile during hospitalization despite supportive measures, prompting workup for infectious triggers of hemolysis.
subjective.past_medical_history: No significant past medical illness. Epidemiological exposure: recent consumption of unpasteurized milk; residing in western India.
subjective.review_of_systems: Fatigue, fever, myalgia, dyspnea. Denied cough, orthopnea, abdominal pain, or weight loss. Home medications: none. Allergies: not documented.

objective.physical_examination: Temperature: febrile, pulse rate: 102 beats/min, blood pressure: 106/70 mmHg. General: pale and clinically icteric. Abdomen: splenomegaly with spleen palpable 2 cm below the left costal margin.
objective.routine_investigations: Complete blood count: severe normocytic anemia with hemoglobin 5.8 g/dL, MCV 92 fL, WBC 3.37 x 103/microL (leukopenia), platelet count 148 x 103/microL. Peripheral blood smear: spherocytes and nucleated red blood cells. Biochemistry: indirect hyperbilirubinemia, elevated lactate dehydrogenase (LDH 1540 IU/L). Reticulocyte panel: corrected reticulocyte count 5.4%. Immunohematology: Direct Coombs test strongly positive (4+). Infectious and autoimmune serologies: HIV, HBsAg, anti-HCV negative; EBV and Mycoplasma serology negative; antinuclear antibodies (ANA) negative.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Acute brucellosis complicated by severe Coombs-positive autoimmune hemolytic anemia (AIHA). Confirmed by blood culture isolating Brucella melitensis and high-titer standard agglutination test (SAT 1 : 640). Viral infections (HIV, HBV, HCV, EBV), Mycoplasma pneumoniae, and primary systemic lupus erythematosus were excluded.
Plan & Outcome: Prescribed oral doxycycline (100 mg twice daily) and rifampicin (600 mg once daily) for 6 weeks, combined with oral prednisolone (1 mg/kg/day). Within one week, hemoglobin rose to 9 g/dL and LDH fell to 988 IU/L. Prednisolone was tapered over 6 weeks. At completion of treatment, hemoglobin normalized to 13 g/dL, and complete remission of hemolytic anemia was maintained at 3-month follow-up.
